Physics benchmarks

Measurements and reference cases used in the 17–18 November 2026 review. Jump to the eleven solver profiles ↓

Equilibria

On the same finite-pressure D-shape input, VMEX and VMEC++ agreed on rotational transform and force residuals. Warm solves took 0.109 s and 0.046 s on the M4. A native DESC solve reduced its independently evaluated force error from 0.408 on the imported fit to 0.00744. On the QUASR 954 vacuum boundary, VMEX edge iota differed from the TORUX coil-surface value by 4.40 × 10⁻⁵.

VMEC++DESC comparison paperTORUX vacuum reference

Fast particles

For 64 matched QA alpha launches over 1 ms, ESSOS, FIRM3D and SIMPLE lost 7, 7 and 6 particles. In ARIES-CS they lost 9, 11 and 12. ESSOS agreed on the fate of 60 of 64 launches with FIRM3D and 55 with SIMPLE. Repeat the individual disagreements at a finer timestep before changing defaults.

ESSOS benchmarkSIMPLEFIRM3DCATAPULT GPU studySTELLOPT / BEAMS3D

Neoclassical transport

On a W7-X surface with 11 × 23 angles and 48 pitch modes, four DKX coefficients differed from native MONKES by at most 1.74%. D33 differed by 0.065%. DKX took 2.58 s cold and 0.096 s warm. The MONKES solve took 0.026 s. This monoenergetic comparison covers a smaller problem than a coupled multispecies solve.

Gyrokinetic turbulence

The archived GKX four-code fixture reports Cyclone heat flux of 6.91 ± 0.19 for GKX and 6.64 ± 0.26 for GX. GS2 and stella have shorter averaging windows. The faster stellarator QA grid shifted flux by 12% against the finer velocity-space reference, so it cannot establish a five-percent result.

GKX, GX, GS2 and stella fixtureGX paperQA resolution study

Edge and duct flow

In a fresh scalar diffusion test, DRBX and Hermes-3 density and pressure differed by at most 3.45 × 10⁻¹⁰. For LMhdX at Ha = 0, the 192 × 64 × 64 duct run gave friction 0.01704 against the DNS target of 0.01714. The wall Nusselt numbers still differed by 3.06%. Heat transfer needs its own refinement test.

DRBX / Hermes-3 casesHermes-3 paperDuct DNS reference

Linear solves

On a constrained 2,305-unknown test, SciPy SuperLU and PETSc/MUMPS solved both the forward and transpose equations to roundoff. On the tested PETSc/SuperLU_DIST build, requesting a transpose solve left a relative residual of 0.424. Factoring the transpose explicitly reduced it below 7 × 10⁻¹⁶. Verify the residual before using a backend for gradients. VMEX, DKX, DRBX, LMhdX, FAX, GKX and MHX declare SOLVAX as a dependency. The 16-right-hand-side gradient test below measures a shared solver component. Each caller still needs its own application check.

PETSc solver manualMUMPS interfaceJAX adjoint contract

Waves and kinetic models

FAX’s QA comparison with the STELLGAP reference gave a mean error of 0.162% for the cosine sector and 0.355% for the sine sector. For particle collisions, use unequal-weight energy and momentum tests alongside the Gauss residual. For SPECTRAX, measure species mass and momentum separately from total energy.

Solver profiles

18 November 2026. Each row names the timed workload and device. Branch comparisons use matching inputs. First calls include compilation.

VMEX

QA equilibrium, 823 iterations

47.87 s first → 3.32 s warm on the A4000. CPU/GPU edge-iota difference 9.8 × 10⁻¹³.

DKX

HSX Fokker–Planck

Reduced case on M4, 30.55 s first → 5.53 s warm. On the shared A4000, the reduced case reached a 1.86 × 10⁻⁹ residual in 22 iterations. The full case exhausted GPU memory with 12.2 GiB sampled process use.

ESSOS

128 QA alphas, 1 ms

18.99 s first → 4.16 s warm on A4000 after field setup. CPU and GPU each lost eight particles.

FAX

CTOK, six global modes

M4 main 0cea7e77 → rebased #66 at 95567b47, 14.02 → 7.29 s first and 0.861 → 0.226 s warm under shared load. All six frequencies matched.

GKX

QA, 96 × 96 × 48, 6 × 12 moments

First 128 attempts took 85.4 s including compilation. Subsequent uncontended chunks took about 31.2 s on A4000.

DRBX

13 four-field RK4 steps

CPU main → #134, 0.349 → 0.108 s per warm step. Full short run took 37.64 → 38.27 s including setup.

LMhdX

Heated duct, RK3 continuation

CPU parent → #332, 10.39 → 2.11 s for the third chunk. Final velocity and temperature matched bit for bit.

JAX-in-Cell

45,000 particles, 200 steps

CPU parent → #86, 9.36 → 4.30 s warm. Four seeds kept the Gauss residual below 8 × 10⁻¹⁵.

On a separate 262,144-particle two-stream test, GPU parent → #80 took 2.069 → 0.778 s warm on a shared A4000. Peak device allocation rose from 166 to 190 MiB. Electric-field histories agreed within 6 × 10⁻¹³ relative.

MHX

128² Orszag–Tang, 400 steps

M4 main → #16, 1.706 → 1.183 s warm. All six physics checks passed on CPU and on a shared A4000.

SPECTRAX

Two-species Orszag–Tang, 40 steps

19.13 s first → 13.25 s warm on M4. Maximum normalized energy drift was 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁶. A shared A4000 finished in 18.04 s first call and 7.50 s warm, with matching final energy.

SOLVAX

16 right-hand sides, reverse derivatives

M4 main → #207, 0.131–0.159 → 0.0415–0.0439 s warm. Directional derivative agreed with a centered check to 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁰.
